resources.string: Fully close any other app that uses the mic\'s PTT: Android delivers the buttons to only one app. On the Abbree, the P1 button makes Android redial the last number; don\'t use it.
For apps that only read a physical key or their on-screen button (BlueDV, Peanut, Mumla, DroidStar). Needs root, and the radio app in the foreground with the screen on.

BlueDV takes 27 (CAMERA), 131 (F1) or 132 (F2) as PTT. In Peanut and Mumla, set their PTT key and press the mic\'s PTT while they wait for it. For the screen point, turn on Developer options › Pointer location and read X/Y on the radio app\'s PTT button.
turn on the accessibility service first

Universal: the bridge looks at the radio app in front (or the last one used) and picks the best way: its PTT intent if it has one (works with the screen off), or holding its on-screen PTT button if you taught it, without root. For apps it does not know, it sends every known PTT intent.
Accessibility service: OFF (needed to know the app in front and to press screen buttons)
None yet. Open the radio app, pull down the notification and tap "Learn PTT button", then tap its PTT button.
Lets PTT Bridge know which app is in the foreground and press a radio app\'s on-screen PTT button while the mic\'s PTT is held. It does not read screen content.
